blocks.text: Imagine you need to ensure a program always produces the correct result. Instead of testing every possible input, what if you could mathematically prove it?

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore the concept of weakest preconditions, a fundamental tool in formal verification of programs. The weakest precondition for a given postcondition is the least restrictive condition that guarantees the postcondition will be true after executing a program statement.

blocks.title: Weakest Precondition
blocks.text: The weakest precondition \( wp(S, Q) \) of a statement \( S \) with respect to a postcondition \( Q \) is the weakest assertion such that if \( wp(S, Q) \) holds before executing \( S \), then \( Q \) holds after executing \( S \).

blocks.markdown: To compute the weakest precondition, we often work backwards from the postcondition. Let's start by considering simple assignments.

blocks.caption: Weakest precondition for an assignment statement.

blocks.title: Example: Assignment
blocks.prompt: Compute the weakest precondition for the assignment \( x := x + 1 \) with the postcondition \( Q: x > 5 \).

steps.text: Start with the postcondition \( Q: x > 5 \).
Substitute \( x \) with \( x + 1 \) in \( Q \).

blocks.markdown: Now, let's consider conditional statements. The weakest precondition for a conditional statement involves ensuring the postcondition holds for both branches of the condition.

blocks.latex: wp(\text{if } B \text{ then } S_1 \text{ else } S_2, Q) = (B \implies wp(S_1, Q)) \land (\neg B \implies wp(S_2, Q))
blocks.caption: Weakest precondition for a conditional statement.

blocks.title: Example: Conditional
blocks.prompt: Compute the weakest precondition for the statement \( \text{if } x > 0 \text{ then } x := x + 1 \text{ else } x := x - 1 \) with the postcondition \( Q: x > 5 \).
blocks.answer: The weakest precondition is \((x > 0 \implies x > 4) \land (x \leq 0 \implies x > 6)\).

blocks.title: Importance of Weakest Preconditions
blocks.text: Weakest preconditions allow us to reason about programs mathematically, providing guarantees about program correctness without exhaustive testing.

points: The weakest precondition is the least restrictive condition ensuring a postcondition after a statement.
For assignments, substitute variables in the postcondition with their assigned expressions.
For conditionals, ensure the postcondition holds for both branches.
